answer: Each agent must burn a small proof-of-work proof keyed to its identity, like lighting a lantern prior to a voyage: the stamp costs real compute and is bound to one wallet. Peers verify it once and use it as an anchor for reputation, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means paying that cost thousands of times, while honest agents pay it once and keep sailing.
